::: {.callout-note}
This record was written from 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-17, before the first tagged release. It describes the code and evidence as they were then, and is kept as history. The [API overview](contracts.qmd) and [verification](verification.qmd) pages describe the current releases.
:::

This pass stabilizes the existing estimators. It adds no model families, backend
interfaces, formula handling, or broader R compatibility. The core remains PHP-free;
the extension converts ordinary arrays and returns complete, synchronous fits.
The [contracts](contracts.qmd), [IDE stubs in the repository](#php-contract-gate),
and offline reference tests define the supported v0.1 surface.

## What the release gate establishes

`PHP=/path/to/php PHP_CONFIG=/matching/php-config ./scripts/check` checks formatting,
Clippy, all Rust tests, an optimized extension build/load, reflected native
signatures/defaults, stubs, ten PHP suites, and every example. The [validation record](verifications/v01-validation.json) captures the exact
source/fixture/binary hashes, executed commands and local software versions.
No R, NumPy,
SciPy or statsmodels is needed for statistical tests or application fitting.
If Python is installed, the gate also checks provenance hashes. A macOS/Linux
GitHub workflow runs the same command; **a configured workflow is not evidence
that those remote platforms have passed**.

This workstation passed 49 Rust tests and nine PHP suites on Apple Silicon,
Rust 1.99 and Homebrew PHP 8.5.10. Seven independent R/Python audit scripts were also rerun successfully,
including the logistic-mixed integrated-likelihood checks. The additional
published-data mode verifies all four Gaussian datasets against lme4, nlme,
statsmodels and the current extension. There are 19 additional deterministic base R
stress fits, checked in both Rust and PHP, alongside the original fixtures.

| Estimator | Supported structure | Offline reference properties | Independent development checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLS | Full-rank fixed design; positive prior weights; offsets | Coefficients, covariance/SE, t/p/CI, fitted/residuals, RSS, R², ML LL; intercept/no-intercept and zero-variance conventions | R lm and statsmodels OLS; weighted/offset R fixtures |
| Logistic | Binary or integer-trial grouped binomial; logit; offsets | Coefficients, inverse-information covariance, normal Wald inference, probability/response residuals, normalized LL, deviance/null deviance/AIC | R glm and statsmodels; weighted/offset R audit |
| Probit | Same binomial input with probit link | Same properties; expected-information covariance | R glm and statsmodels; weighted/offset R audit |
| Poisson | Integer counts; log link; positive prior weights; offsets | Coefficients, inverse-information covariance, Wald inference, means/residuals, normalized LL, deviance/null deviance/AIC | R glm and statsmodels; weighted/offset R audit |
| Fast Gaussian mixed | One grouping factor/random intercept, ML | Fixed inference, covariance, variances, conditional effects, fixed/conditional fits and residuals, LL/AIC | lme4, nlme and statsmodels on synthetic/published data |
| General Gaussian mixed | ML/REML; correlated/independent slopes; multiple crossed/nested terms; weights/offsets | Fixed covariance/inference, term covariance/effects, all fitted/residual vectors, LL/AIC/BIC, singular flags; four R optimizer references | lme4; sleepstudy statsmodels ML/REML; two native optimizers |
| Logistic mixed | One Gaussian random intercept; binary/grouped trials; offsets; Laplace/2–61 AGQ | All fixed inference, group modes/variance, probabilities/residuals, normalized LL/AIC/BIC; 28 same-setting lme4 fits | SciPy independent likelihood/QUADPACK integration, independently optimized cbpp ML, statsmodels GLM boundary reduction |

The [reference manifest](verifications/reference-manifest.json) indexes software
versions actually recorded in fixtures, generators and their hashes, input hashes,
model/options sources, compared quantities and tolerance policies. It does not
invent missing historical package versions or represent old outputs as regenerated.
Fixture values and test sources remain authoritative. Older fixed-model fixtures
record R's version; generator code records family, formula, seed and controls.

## Correctness fixes and compatibility notes

- Single-level logistic/probit now canonicalize accepted integer successes to
  `round(y*trials)/trials`, matching the mixed fitter. Count tolerance is 1e-8.
  Tiny encoded values cannot create fictitious events; all-failure/all-success
  data still fail. Response residuals use canonical proportions.
- Every binomial interface now enforces the previously mixed-only limit of
  **1,000,000 trials per row**, including original rows subsequently dropped.
  This is a deliberate validation tightening: larger-count binomial likelihood
  arithmetic has not been independently verified.
- OLS rejects nonzero residuals whose squared norm/variance underflows, rather
  than returning RSS=0 and an infinite perfect-fit likelihood. Exact zero
  residuals retain the documented infinity/undefined-inference convention.
  Overflowed total/weighted fitted variation now fails explicitly instead of
  leaking a spurious undefined R²; this was reproduced with weighted outcomes
  around 10^155.
- GLMs preserve their ordinary zero-coefficient start. For extreme offsets
  (absolute logit/Poisson offset >20, probit >8) or Poisson counts >10^8,
  an explicit ones column enables a finite marginal intercept fallback. Poisson intercept/exposure arithmetic uses
  log-sum-exp. Tests include constant offsets ±1,000. This does **not** establish
  arbitrary extreme heterogeneous-offset support.
- Poisson log masses for counts at least 16 use deviance plus Stirling error,
  avoiding cancellation between large factorial/log-mean terms. Counts of
  10^12 are checked against R; deviance keeps its existing expm1 calculation.
- Binomial final LL/deviance/AIC receive explicit range checks. Only
  rounding-level negative deviance is rounded to zero; a larger violation
  of saturated likelihood fails.
- Rust errors now carry `ErrorKind`; PHP retains the `Exception` class and adds
  stable codes 1001–1008. Rust `.0` still exposes the message; direct tuple
  construction changes to `StatsError::new(kind, message)`.
- Successful result arrays gain **diagnostics**; existing top-level keys and
  PHP signatures/defaults remain. Strict consumers must allow the additional key.
  Missing-row warnings are still emitted once and also recorded in diagnostics.
  The two internal PHP-boundary `expect` calls were removed. ext-php-rs's handler
  catches Rust unwinding panics, but allocation failure/process abort is not
  recoverable; no memory-safety guarantee is inferred from ordinary unit tests.

See [diagnostic/error definitions](contracts.qmd#v01-diagnostics-and-errors).

## Stress tests and numerical limits

`tests/fixtures/stress-r.json` records each design, response, weight, offset,
reference specification, R version and tolerance. It tests near collinearity,
columns in different units, outcomes scaled by 10^-140 and 10^140, tiny positive
residual variance, weighted/no-intercept estimation, rare outcomes, ±1,000
constant offsets, sparse Poisson outcomes and 10^12 counts. Known ±1,000 binary predictors
with balanced non-extreme observations remain valid (R saturation warnings are
recorded), and a no-intercept Poisson model tests known means down to exp(-500).

Absolute tolerances are expressed in response units: for scaled OLS estimates,
SE/CI/fits/residuals they multiply response_scale, and for covariance its square.
Dimensionless statistics and log likelihood are not rescaled. This avoids
requiring relative accuracy in covariance entries whose mathematical value is
zero. The nearly collinear fixture uses a disclosed 1e-6 relative tolerance;
this does not relax the original, well-conditioned reference suite.

Existing tests retain exact rank deficiency, complete/quasi separation, nonfinite
and invalid inputs, zero/invalid weights, exhausted budgets, legitimate variance
boundaries, correlated slopes, nested/crossed and four-level Gaussian designs,
ML/REML, predictor-unit invariance, and quadrature tail-weight stability.
The new dense-limit test rejects q=513 before factorization.

Limitations remain:

- Numerical inputs become f64, with a 53-bit significand. Integer-valued inputs
  beyond 2^53 can lose exactness during PHP-to-Rust conversion; arbitrary-precision
  count/design arithmetic is not supported. The stress checks do not establish
  accuracy for every representable count or input magnitude.

- Full rank at floating-point precision does not imply well-conditioned inference.
  Separation detection is a direction certificate, not a complete linear-programming
  proof. Finite uncertain estimates can be valid; difficult problems may fail
  rank, line-search, arithmetic or iteration checks.
- General Gaussian computation is dense: q≤512 and n(q+p+1)≤50,000,000, excluding
  additional temporary matrices and PHP arrays. These are guards, not a memory
  reservation or sparse-solver capability. No new general-mixed performance claim
  is inferred from the fast specialization.
- General Gaussian convergence uses native optimizer termination/bounds and
  finite factors/outputs. A final gradient/Hessian convergence audit of variance
  parameters is **not implemented**; diagnostics do not fabricate one. Multi-start
  global optimality is not established. Use reference comparisons and start/optimizer
  sensitivity for difficult fits.
- Gaussian inference uses plug-in GLS covariance and normal Wald tests, not
  Satterthwaite/Kenward–Roger corrections. REML criteria depend on the fixed
  design and should not compare models with different fixed-effect columns.
- Logistic mixed inference uses joint observed information of the chosen
  approximate likelihood. Its score gate and positive Hessian are numerical
  checks, not approximation-accuracy proofs. Tau≤20, scaled beta bounds±100,
  one grouping term, integer trials and max61 AGQ remain explicit limits.
- In the rare-event fixture, Laplace estimates group SD≈7.30 while 61 nodes
  give ≈3.36. Agreement with lme4 at one node does not establish accuracy.
  [The integration notebook](notebooks/logistic-mixed-verification.qmd) retains
  the independent error checks and explains grouped-binomial likelihood constants.
- Missing values use listwise deletion; this is a data policy, not an assumption
  that missingness is ignorable or that deletion produces unbiased inference.

## PHP contract gate

`stubs/phit.php` is for IDE/static-analysis indexing, **not runtime inclusion**.
Generate it with the extension loaded:

```sh
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" scripts/php-stubs.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" scripts/php-stubs.php --check
```

The generator reads actual native argument types/names/defaults via Reflection.
`tests/fixtures/php-api.json` freezes those signatures and expected result keys;
`tests/stability.php` fits every estimator and checks result keys and diagnostic
aliases. Updating the API fixture requires an explicit `--write-api`, which should
only follow compatibility review. Structured PHPDoc documents matrix vectors,
group types, random terms and per-function return shapes. ext-php-rs also offers
[its official cargo-php stub workflow](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/cargo-php.html);
our maintained declarations additionally include result-array shapes.

## Performance preservation

The saved pre-audit binary was compared with the stabilized binary using the same
inputs, runtime, five complete timed fits after warm-up, and single-thread environment.
Every numerical comparison passed. Timings include PHP input conversion and full
result materialization; JSON serialization is outside timed fitting. Whole-process
RSS includes runtime/startup/serialization. There is one local measurement batch,
so small percentage differences in millisecond fits are not evidence of regressions
or speed improvements. No matrix backend or Gaussian square-root path was replaced.

Targeted investigation caught a 100,000-row Poisson regression during this pass:
an unconditional marginal-intercept start took 61 iterations instead of six,
with negligible estimate differences but a roughly 16-fold slowdown. It was
restricted to extreme inputs where the zero start is unsafe. The final report
also records iteration/evaluation counts. This preserves the existing ordinary
iteration path and avoids treating a theoretically helpful start as an optimization.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import json
import pandas as pd

from IPython.display import display
ROOT=next(p for p in [Path.cwd(),*Path.cwd().parents] if (p/'Cargo.toml').exists())
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT/'docs/figures'))
from bridge import render_figure
r=json.loads((ROOT/'docs/benchmarks/v01-preservation-results.json').read_text())
rows=[]
for c in r['cases']:
    for label in ['baseline','v01']:
        v=c['implementations'][label]
        rows.append(dict(model=c['model'],observations=c['n'],implementation=label,
                         median_full_fit_seconds=v['median_fit_seconds'],
                         minimum_full_fit_seconds=v['min_fit_seconds'],
                         peak_process_MiB=v['peak_rss_bytes']/2**20,
                         numerical_agreement=c['numerical_agreement']))
t=pd.DataFrame(rows);display(t)
render_figure('preservation')
print('Measured binary hashes:',r['baseline_sha256'],r['extension_sha256'])
```

The [full report](benchmarks/v01-preservation-results.json) records hashes,
versions, samples, all errors, timings and memory. Reproducing a before/after
comparison requires retaining the old compiled extension and using
`tests/benchmarks/run-v01.py --baseline /path/to/old/library`.
Historical R/Python benchmark reports remain historical measurements with their
original hashes; they are not relabeled as this binary's performance. Current
R/Python correctness audits are separate from performance preservation.

## Release readiness and remaining gates

The native functions, offline statistical suite and examples work on the tested
macOS/PHP combination. This is a **release candidate**, not a claim of universal
production readiness and not a published release.

Before distribution:

1. Run the new CI on Linux and macOS and record results; exercise each PHP/SAPI,
   architecture and ZTS/NTS combination advertised as supported. PHP 8.3+ is the
   intended consumer range, but this pass executed PHP 8.5.10 CLI only.
2. Preserve the root MIT LICENSE and the separate notices/provenance for bundled
   reference data and third-party assets when preparing distribution packages.
3. Review diagnostics, input tightening and the retained numerical limits against
   application requirements. Confirm FPM headers/build ABI and restart workers
   after installation; a CLI load does not verify web-server deployment.
4. Choose release metadata/distribution packaging and publish through the project's
   release workflow. This pass does not create a tag, commit, push or package release.

No full R/lme4 compatibility promise is made. New families, inference methods,
sparse general mixed computation and broader GLMM designs are outside this pass.

## Review follow-up

A subsequent source review found obsolete exclusions in the contracts page and
three PHP validation paths that emitted uncoded Exception instances. Those paths
now use the same typed 1001 code for out-of-range binomial outcomes, invalid Poisson
counts and invalid group IDs. The group parser is shared rather than duplicated.
Regression tests check codes for logistic/probit, both simple mixed calls and
general Gaussian mixed grouping, including invalid values on rows that would
otherwise be dropped. Statistical algorithms and public signatures are unchanged.

The [first GitHub CI run](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/actions/runs/38188972784)
failed during macOS binding generation with incompatible Clang ARM builtin headers;
Linux was cancelled by matrix fail-fast. The workflow now aligns Homebrew compiler,
libclang and resource headers, and lets both platforms finish independently. This
configuration change passes the full local gate with the aligned LLVM toolchain:
49 Rust tests, nine PHP suites and all seven examples. It still needs a successful
remote run and is not Linux numerical verification. The original local validation
record remains a dated snapshot.

An optional constrained first-order/curvature audit for general Gaussian variance
parameters remains future work. Optimizer termination and verified stationarity
are distinct; the current contract does not claim the latter. No strict stationarity
option, prediction-only interface or new model family is introduced in this follow-up.

## Fixed-intercept API update

All PHP fitters now append `intercept: true` by default. Application inputs contain
predictors only, with an estimated fixed intercept returned first. Existing callers
that supplied ones must remove that column or pass `intercept: false` to preserve
the literal design. The Rust core and general mixed-model random designs remain
explicit matrices. `tests/intercept.php` verifies exact equivalence for all seven
families, intercept-only and through-origin fits, and Poisson log-exposure offsets
against both closed-form calculations and stored R fixtures. Stubs and reflected
API fixtures include the appended option. See [the contract](contracts.qmd#fixed-intercept-convention-and-migration).

After this API update, the complete gate passed 49 Rust tests, ten PHP suites, and
all eight examples on the configured Apple Silicon/PHP workstation. The earlier
validation JSON records the preceding nine-suite run rather than this new check.

The [v0.2 readiness assessment](v0.2.qmd) records the distribution, descriptive
and draw-matrix additions and their own verification/performance evidence. The
v0.1 results above remain the historical fitting baseline. Current release

## Installation and release packaging

The [deployment guide](deployment.qmd) documents local PIE support, a pinned
multi-stage PHP-FPM container, a versioned source/binary artifact workflow and
actual installation checks. The registered module is now `phit` to satisfy
PIE's naming rules; function names remain unchanged. Public registry/release
publication is pending.

The [packaging record](verifications/packaging-results.json) captures Linux
Bookworm/aarch64 PHP 8.3.35, 8.4.26 and 8.5.11, including actual CLI and FPM requests,
plus macOS/arm64 PHP 8.5.10 staging/loading. Each complete gate passes 56 Rust
tests, 11 PHP suites and eight examples. The added distribution suite checks
8,618 points with the original tolerances, using independent stored references
where R differs; scaled-density underflow and API snapshot float typing were
fixed. Source-archive installation and extracted binary loading pass. The
configured amd64 CI matrix still needs a remote run before release publication.
